chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn who said:

I asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) for a supplication while I was behind him, so he said: 'O Allah, I ask You by Your Noble Face, and Your Great Name, and by Your Might which cannot be reached, and by Your Power from which nothing is prevented, that You do such and such with me.'

He said, 'And he wrote to me a note in his own handwriting: Say, O He who is Exalted so He Dominates, and Hidden so He Knows, O He who is King so He is Powerful, and O He who Revives the Dead, and He is Able over all things. Send blessings upon Muhammad and the Family of Muhammad, and do such and such with me. Then say, O There is no god but Allah, have mercy on me by the right of 'There is no god but Allah', have mercy on me.'

And he wrote to me in another note, instructing me to say: 'O Allah, ward off from me by Your Might and Your Strength. O Allah, I ask You for Your blessings in this day of mine, and this month of mine, and this year of mine, and this month of mine, and whatever descends therein of punishment, or disliked events, or affliction, so turn it away from me and from my children by Your Might and Your Strength. Indeed, You are Able over all things.'

O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the fading of Your blessings, and the changing of Your well-being, and from the suddenness of Your retribution, and from the evil of the writing (of deeds) that has preceded. O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the evil of myself, and from the evil of every creature, You are the Seizer of its forelock. Indeed, You are Able over all things, and indeed Allah has encompassed all things in knowledge, and counted all things with a count.

key_terms.صَلِّ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ وَ آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ: Send blessings upon Muhammad and the Family of Muhammad

ai.seo_question: What is the supplication for distress and worries taught by Imam Al-Rida?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi, this supplication emphasizes invoking Allah through His supreme attributes of glory and omnipotence, reflecting the Shia tradition of using divine names as a means of spiritual connection. It integrates specific petitions for protection from sudden calamities and the decay of blessings, culminating in a reminder of Allah's comprehensive knowledge and enumeration of all things.
